title: Customer feedback: rapid gist + low-touch burndown (Mar 12 2026)
content:
TL;DR: Shortlist of small, fast-to-deliver fixes and a prioritized burndown for customer-facing runtime and API pain points. Focus: reduce token-level latency outliers, simplify retry/workaround patterns customers use, and unblock a set of high-frequency asks with low engineering cost. Notes are terse — use as a sprint-ready starter pack.

Top recurring customer asks (rough frequency + exemplar):
- Deterministic fallback policy for heavy tails (reported by 7 customers) — customers want automatic downgrade to cheaper model variant when latency spikes. Example: ecommerce search reranker spikes when prompt length > 512.
- Easier prefix caching controls (11 customers) — desire for a simple toggle or TTL rather than manual KV management. Many hacky client-side workarounds observed.
- More transparent token/embedding billing snippets (9 customers) — customers spend time reconciling tokens with embeddings calls in multiplexed flows.
- Per-route rate-limit visibility & debug hooks (5 customers) — want call-level traces showing which policy fired.
- One-click dev-mode for private deployments (3 customers) — a temporary dev-mode with verbose logs & sample workload generator.

Severity matrix (operational + customer impact):
- P0: Latency tail causing user-visible timeouts (3 customers reporting weekly outages) — quick mitigation: add an explicit canary throttle + fallback to 1x smaller model.
- P1: Billing confusion for embeddings in batched pipelines — leads to churn risk and multiple support tickets.
- P2: UX friction around prefix caching controls — high annoyance but low immediate revenue risk.

Low-touch quick fixes (<= 2 engineer-weeks):
1) Canary fallback flag (API): config toggle per-route to enable automatic variant fallback. Deliverable: API param + server-side simple policy, telemetry event. Tickets: CUST-4231.
2) Dev-mode installer script for Private: one-script that flips logging to DEBUG, mounts sample traffic generator; gated behind enterprise consent. Deliverable: bash installer + README.
3) Billing snippet guides: short doc + SDK example showing token vs embedding cost breakdowns for common pipelines. Deliverable: doc + 2 SDK examples.
4) Expose rate-limit decision trace: return header X-RateDecision: <policy-id> and a trace id customers can send. Deliverable: header + minimal trace endpoint.

Longer proposals (>= 3 engineer-weeks):
- Unified prefix cache UI: Console control with TTL histogram + autopopulate suggestions based on recent traffic.
- Cost-aware routing policy: runtime chooses model variant by expected token cost vs latency SLA.

Risk notes & customer workarounds observed:
- Several customers shard requests to multiple shorter prompts to avoid KV cache thrash — increases token count and cost.
- Some customers implement client-side model fallback, duplicating requests (costly). Exposing a server-side policy will reduce waste.

Suggested sprint plan (2-week cycle):
Week A:
- Spike + simple API spec for canary fallback (owner: Connor Lee).
- Draft billing snippet doc and SDK sample (owner: Sofia Martinez).
Week B:
- Implement header-based rate decision trace and add telemetry (owner: Devon Chen).
- Demo dev-mode script for Private (owner: Aisha Patel).

Acceptance criteria (for quick fixes):
- Canary fallback: 95th percentile latency for affected flows reduced OR error-rate fallback observed in telemetry.
- Billing docs: reduction in billing-related support threads for pilot customers.
- Rate-decision header: support can reproduce a policy decision within 24h of receiving trace id.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should canary fallback be on by default for hosted API or opt-in? (ops sensitivity)
- What SLA delta is acceptable when downgrading model variant? (product/legal)

Immediate asks for PM/Eng sync:
- Quick prioritization for canary fallback (estimated 6–10 dev-days).
- Identify 2 pilot customers willing to test dev-mode and billing doc (we have 3 volunteers: AcmeCommerce, NotaTech, LexiAI).

Notes to self: keep language non-prescriptive in customer-facing docs; provide explicit examples and small code snippets. This doc is a rapid synthesis — use it to seed a Confluence page and a 2-sprint delivery plan.
summary: Concise synthesis of customer feedback into a shortlist of small fixes (canary fallback, dev-mode script, billing snippets, rate-decision trace) plus a 2-week sprint plan and acceptance criteria. Prioritize latency tail mitigation and billability clarity.
next_steps: Sync w/ PM (Priya) and Eng-Infra on toggle semantics by 2026-03-18
Create Jira epic CUST-4231 and link quick-fix tasks
Email pilot customers with invite to trial dev-mode
notes: Document telemetry events for each quick-fix
Measure ticket volume change post-doc publish
